knowledge_tree.title: Selective Compulsory English Book 4
knowledge_tree.content: A comprehensive English textbook for senior high school students, covering themes like science fiction, iconic attractions, sea exploration, sharing, and career launching.

children.title: Unit 1: SCIENCE FICTION
children.content: Explores themes of robotics, AI, time travel, and their implications on human society.

children.title: Reading and Thinking: Satisfaction Guaranteed
children.content: A story by Isaac Asimov about a domestic robot named Tony and its interactions with a human family, exploring human-robot relationships.

children.title: Characters in the Story
children.content: Larry Belmont, Claire, Tony, Gladys Claffern - their roles and relationships.

children.title: Themes and Analysis
children.content: Human emotions towards robots, ethical considerations of AI, and potential future scenarios.

children.title: Learning About Language
children.content: Focus on vocabulary building, passive voice, and past participles.

children.title: Build Up Your Vocabulary
children.content: Key terms: fiction, test out, bonus, more like, ridiculous, integrity, dignity, etc.

children.title: Review Useful Structures
children.content: Passive voice usage and examples from the text.

children.title: Using Language
children.content: Listening and speaking activities about robots and AI, and writing a sci-fi short story.

children.title: Listening: Robots and AI
children.content: Interview with a sci-fi expert discussing benefits and risks of advanced robotics.

children.title: Writing a Sci-Fi Short Story
children.content: Based on 'The Time Machine' by H.G. Wells, encouraging creative writing about time travel.

children.title: Project: Design a Robot or AI Device
children.content: Group project to create and present an original robot or AI concept.

children.title: Unit 2: ICONIC ATTRACTIONS
children.content: Focuses on cultural and natural landmarks, particularly in Australia, and descriptive writing.

children.title: Reading and Thinking: Volunteering in the Bush
children.content: A blog by Jo about her teaching experience in Papua New Guinea, highlighting cultural differences and challenges.

children.title: Cultural Insights
children.content: Description of local customs, housing, food, and community life in a remote village.

children.title: Educational Challenges
children.content: Lack of resources, adapting teaching methods, and the value of education in underserved areas.

children.title: Learning About Language
children.content: Vocabulary related to travel and culture, and the use of past participles.

children.title: Build Up Your Vocabulary
children.content: Terms like iconic, foundation, political, didgeridoo, located, equator, etc.

children.title: Review Useful Structures
children.content: Past participles as attributes, adverbials, predicatives, and object complements.

children.title: Using Language
children.content: Listening about New Zealand's attractions and writing a description of an iconic animal.

children.title: Listening: Amazing New Zealand
children.content: Radio program discussing what best represents New Zealand (e.g., geothermal parks, Bay of Islands).

children.title: Writing: Describe an Iconic Animal
children.content: Based on Australian animals like kangaroos, koalas, and Tasmanian devils, using rhetorical devices.

children.title: Project: Introduce an Iconic Attraction
children.content: Research and present a local iconic attraction from your city or town.

children.title: Unit 3: SEA EXPLORATION
children.content: Covers historical and modern sea exploration, environmental issues, and argumentative writing.

children.title: Reading and Thinking: Reaching Out Across the Sea
children.content: Discusses historical sea voyages (e.g., Zheng He, Marco Polo) and modern initiatives like the Belt and Road.

children.title: Historical Explorers
children.content: Zheng He's voyages, Silk Road, and their impact on trade and cultural exchange.

children.title: Modern Context
children.content: Belt and Road Initiative, Arctic exploration, and scientific research on climate change.

children.title: Learning About Language
children.content: Vocabulary related to exploration and the use of infinitives.

children.title: Build Up Your Vocabulary
children.content: Terms: tale, merchant, set sail, extend, negotiate, fleet, behold, league, etc.

children.title: Review Useful Structures
children.content: Infinitives as subject, predicative, object, complement, attribute, and adverbial.

children.title: Using Language
children.content: Listening about whale research and writing an argumentative essay on sea exploration.

children.title: Listening: Whale Watching Camp
children.content: Conversation about whale species, research methods, and conservation efforts.

children.title: Writing an Argumentative Essay
children.content: Presenting arguments for and against sea exploration, using the PEEL method (Point, Evidence, Explanation, Link).

children.title: Project: Create a Poster for World Oceans Day
children.content: Design a poster to raise awareness about ocean conservation.

children.title: Unit 4: SHARING
children.content: Focuses on volunteering, global aid, and speech writing.

children.title: Reading and Thinking: Volunteering in the Bush
children.content: Further details from Jo's blog about her experiences in Papua New Guinea.

children.title: Living Conditions
children.content: Description of the village, housing, food preparation, and local beliefs.

children.title: Personal Reflections
children.content: Jo's feelings about her volunteer work and the impact on her perspective.

children.title: Learning About Language
children.content: Vocabulary related to volunteering and community service, and the use of phrases.

children.title: Build Up Your Vocabulary
children.content: Terms: parcel, jam, mail, secondary, clay, dust, weed, chorus, etc.

children.title: Review Useful Structures
children.content: Noun phrases, verb phrases, adverbial phrases, adjective phrases, and prepositional phrases.

children.title: Using Language
children.content: Listening about volunteer opportunities and giving a speech about China's aid to other countries.

children.title: Listening: Student Volunteers
children.content: Discussion about types of volunteer work and how to get involved.

children.title: Giving a Speech
children.content: Based on a transcript about China's aid projects, focusing on structure and rhetorical questions.

children.title: Project: Create a Poster for Volunteer Work
children.content: Design a poster to promote a volunteer organization or event.

children.title: Unit 5: LAUNCHING YOUR CAREER
children.content: Covers career planning, university majors, and job applications.

children.title: Reading and Thinking: Working Out What You Want to Do
children.content: Discusses the importance of career planning and using aptitude tests to find suitable careers.

children.title: Career Aptitude Tests
children.content: How they work, the types of questions, and how to interpret results (e.g., RIASEC model).

children.title: Career Suggestions
children.content: Matching personality types (Realistic, Investigative, Artistic, Social, Enterprising, Conventional) to potential jobs.

children.title: Learning About Language
children.content: Vocabulary related to careers and education, and the use of long sentences.

children.title: Build Up Your Vocabulary
children.content: Terms: bounce, head start, aptitude, scenario, lawyer, assemble, drawer, etc.

children.title: Review Useful Structures
children.content: Compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences for effective communication.

children.title: Using Language
children.content: Listening about choosing university majors and writing an application letter and CV.

children.title: Listening: Choosing a University Major
children.content: Conversation about factors to consider when selecting a major and university.

children.title: Writing an Application Letter and CV
children.content: Based on a job advertisement for a summer camp helper, focusing on structure and content.

children.title: Project: Make a Speech About Your Future Career
children.content: Prepare and deliver a speech about your career goals and plans.
